person.name: Frank_Lloyd_Wright
person.summary: Frank Lloyd Wright was an American architect who developed buildings around their sites, materials, and daily use. His Prairie houses, Usonian homes, public buildings, and architectural school shaped American design across seven decades.

conclusion: In 2019, eight Wright buildings, including Fallingwater, Unity Temple, and the Guggenheim Museum, were inscribed as The 20th-Century Architecture of Frank Lloyd Wright, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Museums and preservation organizations maintain many of his buildings across the United States.

events.title: Born into a Wisconsin Unitarian Family
events.description: Frank Lloyd Wright was born in Richland Center, Wisconsin, to William Cary Wright and Anna Lloyd Jones Wright. William was a musician, speaker, and occasional preacher. Anna was a schoolteacher from the Welsh American Lloyd Jones family. The household included William's Baptist ministry and Anna's Unitarian relatives.

events.title: Studies Civil Engineering in Madison
events.description: In 1886, Frank Lloyd Wright entered the University of Wisconsin in Madison as a special student. He studied civil engineering under professor Allan D. Conover before leaving the university without taking a degree.

events.title: Begins Apprenticeship at Adler and Sullivan
events.description: In 1887, Frank Lloyd Wright left Joseph Lyman Silsbee's Chicago office. He joined Adler & Sullivan as a draftsman and apprentice. Louis Sullivan assigned him interior drawings for the [[Auditorium Building|Auditorium Building]]. Dankmar Adler was the firm's senior partner.

images.caption: Auditorium Building, designed by Adler and Sullivan
images.creator: Cornell University Library

Auditorium Building.explanation: The Auditorium Building was a Chicago complex with a theater, hotel, offices, and a tower. Adler & Sullivan designed it while Wright worked in the firm.

events.background:
The opening was tied to a large interior-design job. Wright could translate Sullivan’s ornament into finished drawings, and that skill secured his place after two brief interviews. The office was difficult from the start. Wright recalled violent clashes with other draftsmen during his early years there. He also said Sullivan treated employees with little respect.

Sullivan nevertheless gave Wright increasing responsibility. Wright developed a close working relationship with the foreman Paul Mueller, who later worked on several of Wright’s public and commercial buildings. By 1890, Wright was head draftsman for the firm’s houses. He shared an office beside Sullivan’s with George Elmslie, a draftsman Wright had recommended for the staff.

events.title: Launches an Independent Chicago Practice
events.description: In 1893, Louis Sullivan discovered that Frank Lloyd Wright had accepted independent residential commissions against his contract. Wright left Adler & Sullivan. He opened his practice on the top floor of Chicago's Schiller Building, which Sullivan had designed.

events.title: Moves Practice into Oak Park Studio
events.description: In 1898, Frank Lloyd Wright moved his practice into a studio addition beside his Oak Park home. Its two-story drafting room had a hanging balcony. The larger space let him employ several draftsmen on new residential designs.

images.caption: Frank Lloyd Wright Home and Studio, Oak Park
images.creator: Bmzuckerman

events.title: Designs Oak Park's Unity Temple
events.description: A fire destroyed the Oak Park Unitarian congregation's church. The congregation asked Frank Lloyd Wright to design Unity Temple. He worked on it from 1905 to 1909. He used [[reinforced concrete|concrete strengthened with internal steel]] for a compact worship space and connected community rooms.

images.caption: Unity Temple exterior, Oak Park, Illinois

reinforced concrete.explanation: Reinforced concrete combines concrete with internal steel reinforcement, allowing a structure to carry loads with thinner walls and broader open spaces.

events.background: Wright belonged to the Unity Temple congregation throughout his life. He offered to design its replacement after the earlier church burned. He later described Unity Temple as the building where he became “an architect of space.”

background_images.caption: Built in 1905-1908, this Prairie-style building was designed by Frank Lloyd Wright for the congregation of the Unity Church of Oak Park, founded in 1871, and re.

events.title: Publishes the Wasmuth Portfolio in Berlin
events.description: In Berlin, publisher Ernst Wasmuth issued the Wasmuth Portfolio, Wright's first publication. The two-volume portfolio collected plans and line drawings for buildings Wright designed between 1893 and 1909.

images.caption: Robie House plate from the Wasmuth Portfolio

event_class.title: Ausgeführte Bauten und Entwürfe von Frank Lloyd Wright
event_class.impact: The portfolio brought Wright's designs to architects in Germany and the Netherlands and informed European debates about modern architecture.

events.title: Builds Taliesin in Spring Green
events.description: In 1911, Frank Lloyd Wright left Chicago for Spring Green, Wisconsin. He began building Taliesin on land his mother, Anna Lloyd Jones Wright, had bought in the Lloyd Jones family valley. Mamah Borthwick returned to the United States in June. She joined Wright at Taliesin in August while construction continued.

events.title: Fire and Murders at Taliesin
events.description: On August 15, 1914, Frank Lloyd Wright was in Chicago overseeing work on Midway Gardens, an entertainment complex he designed. At Taliesin near Spring Green, Julian Carlton set fire to the living quarters. Carlton killed Mamah Borthwick, John and Martha Cheney, David Lindblom, Emil Brodelle, Thomas Brunker, and Ernest Weston. William Weston and Thomas Fritz survived, and Carlton was jailed after attempting suicide.
events.background:
Taliesin had drawn hostile attention since Wright and Borthwick began living there in 1911. The Spring Green Weekly Home News condemned Wright. Chicago newspapers suggested that he might be arrested for immorality. The local sheriff said he could prove no wrongdoing. The controversy affected Wright's work for several years. Midway Gardens became his next major commission in 1913.

Carlton had been hired as a Taliesin servant several months before the attack. He used a roofing hatchet or a similar shingling tool against people fleeing the burning residence. Thomas Fritz survived. William Weston was injured. He helped put out the fire, which nearly destroyed the residential wing.

Carlton hid after the attack and swallowed hydrochloric acid in an attempt to kill himself. People who found him nearly lynched him. He was taken to the Dodgeville jail. He died of starvation seven weeks later despite medical attention. Borthwick was buried at Unity Chapel near Taliesin.

events.title: Designs the Imperial Hotel in Tokyo
events.description: In 1915, Frank Lloyd Wright began designing Tokyo's Imperial Hotel. His son, John Lloyd Wright, accompanied him and helped oversee the project. The design used interlocking beams intended to improve the building's safety during earthquakes.

events.title: Marries Olgivanna Lazović in California
events.description: On August 25, 1928, Frank Lloyd Wright married Olgivanna Lazović in Rancho Santa Fe, California. They had met in Chicago in November 1924. Wright invited her to tea after they met at a dance performance.

locations.name_modern: Rancho Santa Fe, California, United States

events.title: Creates the Taliesin Fellowship Community
events.description: In 1932, Frank Lloyd Wright and Olgivanna Wright established the Taliesin Fellowship at Taliesin in Spring Green, Wisconsin. It was a residential apprenticeship community for architecture. Fellows lived and worked with Wright, studied architecture and spiritual development, and helped operate the estate.

events.title: Designs Fallingwater for the Kaufmanns
events.description: In 1935, Edgar J. Kaufmann commissioned Frank Lloyd Wright to design Fallingwater, a weekend house for the Kaufmann family at Bear Run in rural Pennsylvania. Wright placed the house directly above the waterfall and arranged concrete terraces over the stream.
events.background:
Kaufmann's work with Wright in 1935 also included executive offices on the top floor of his Pittsburgh department store. Loja Saarinen designed the office's carpet and textiles. Edgar Kaufmann Jr. later gave the Kaufmann Office to the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.

The design and construction of Fallingwater involved a complex process. Wright and Kaufmann developed a distinctive relationship as architect and patron during it. The house's success revived Wright's career after the Great Depression.

events.title: Designs S. C. Johnson Headquarters
events.description: In 1936, Herbert Fisk Johnson hired Frank Lloyd Wright to design headquarters for the S. C. Johnson company in Racine, Wisconsin. Wright planned a brick office building around a great workroom. Slender concrete columns widened at the top to support the room.

images.caption: Johnson Wax Headquarters, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright
images.creator: Bmzuckerman

events.title: Accepts Guggenheim Museum Design Commission
events.description: In 1943, Solomon R. Guggenheim hired Frank Lloyd Wright to design a New York City museum for his collection of [[nonobjective art|nonobjective art]]. Wright developed a circular gallery. Visitors would follow a continuous interior ramp through the building.

locations.name_modern: New York City, New York, United States

images.caption: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York City
images.creator: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA

nonobjective art.explanation: Nonobjective art does not depict recognizable people, places, or objects. Guggenheim collected this form of abstraction.

events.background: The design process lasted 16 years. Wright produced 700 sketches and six sets of working drawings before the museum opened in 1959.

events.title: Dies After Surgery in Phoenix
events.description: Frank Lloyd Wright was hospitalized in Phoenix after abdominal surgery. He died there on April 9, 1959, at age 91.
